resources.string: A mode is a group of overrides: the emoji row, the pinned tools and the symbol sets. A mode turns on automatically for the apps or the field types you select, for example password boxes and email boxes. You can also turn a mode on by hand from the Modes tool on the keyboard.
Let apps and field types switch the keyboard setup

Modes are on by default. When they are on, the keyboard changes its emoji row, its pinned tools and its symbol sets to match the app or the field you are typing in. Turn this off to use one setup everywhere. Your modes are kept, so turning it back on restores all of them.
Modes are off. The keyboard uses the same setup in every app. The modes below are kept and take effect again when you turn modes back on.
The keyboard saves a drag into the mode that is on

A mode that has its own pinned tools or toolbox order wins over the global lists while the mode is active. With this setting on, the keyboard writes the new tool order back into that mode. The change stays where you made it, and the apps on a different mode keep their own arrangement. With this setting off, a drag always changes the global order, and the list of the mode continues to override it.
The tool order can be different in each app. The mode that matches an app decides the order you see there.
The Modes tool shows this name
The Modes tool shows this icon beside the name
Inherit the theme that is set

While this mode is active, the keyboard uses this theme. It replaces the theme you set elsewhere, and it also replaces an automatic light and dark pair for the time the mode runs. The mode does not change your own choice. Your theme comes back when the mode ends.
Change the pinned tools of the toolbar while this mode is active
The keyboard adds these tools after the tools you pinned yourself
Only these tools are pinned while this mode is active
Move the tools of this mode to the front of the toolbox panel
The tools you select come first in the toolbox. The other tools keep their usual place behind them.
The symbol row shows only the sets of this mode while it is active
The row opens on the first set in the order.
Both conditions must match. This mode turns on only for these field types in the apps in the list below.
This mode turns on when you select a field in the app
One of the field types above must also match
Remove this app from the mode

If you set apps and field types together, both must match. For example, bind a mode to your chat apps and to the Text field type. The mode then stays off the search boxes of those apps. If you set only one of the two, the mode matches on that one alone. If you set neither, you can turn the mode on only by hand. When more than one mode matches, a mode that names field types wins over a mode that names only apps. A password box in a code editor still gets the password mode. A mode that you select by hand from the Modes tool wins until you change apps.
The mode goes back to the pinned tools, the toolbox order, the symbol row, the apps and the field types that it ships with. The app deletes your changes to the mode.
The mode and everything set up inside it goes, including its apps, its pinned tools and any overrides. This cannot be undone.
A mode you pick by hand
How long it stays on after you choose it

This is about picking a mode yourself from the Modes tool, not about a mode that switches on for an app on its own. Until you change app is the keyboard\'s old behaviour and suits a mode you reach for once. Until you change it suits a mode you meant to stay in, and it stays on until you pick another mode or turn it off.
Which layout this mode types on

The mode wears this layout while it is on, whichever layout you were using before. Your own layout comes back when the mode ends, and the spacebar swipe order is not changed. Only layouts you have switched on are offered here; if you later switch one off, a mode that used it goes back to inheriting.
